newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Trial for ex-Rio policeman in massacre of children.
newsitem.headline: Trial for ex-Rio policeman in massacre of children.

text.p: A former policeman who voluntarily confessed his role in the killing of eight street children near a Rio de Janeiro church more than three years ago is due to go on trial on Wednesday, court officials said.

Nelson Oliveira dos Santos Cunha, who resigned from the Rio police force after the massacre, confessed to taking part in the killings just days before the first of four men accused of participating in the massacre went on trial last April.

Three policemen and one civilian were arrested shortly after the killings and accused of firing indiscriminately at about 70 children playing or sleeping on the steps of the Candelaria Church in the centre of Rio early on July 23, 1993.
Six children died at the church, and the bodies of two more were later found nearby.

Cunha, a recently born-again Christian who said he felt deep remorse, implicated three other men during his eight-hour confession. One was police officer Marcus Vinicius Borges Emmanuel, tried and convicted in April. Another is awaiting trial, and the third was murdered in 1994.
Cunha's confession will be contested at Wednesday's trial by Wagner dos Santos, one of the survivors of the shooting spree and the key witness in Emmanuel's trial.
Santos returned to Rio on Monday from Switzerland, where he fled after two attempts on his life after the killings. He had been under federal police protection since his return.
Cristina Leonardo, Santos' lawyer, said Wednesday's trial was "fundamental," because her client's version of events conflicted with Cunha's account of the Candelaria massacre.

She said Santos did not recognise Cunha as one of the killers, although Cunha said he was the one who shot and wounded Santos. Cunha says the man Santos identified as his main attacker, former police officer Carlos Jorge Liaffa, did not take part in the killings. Liaffa was released and never charged because of Cunha's testimony, Leonardo said.
On the day of the massacre, Santos was bundled into a car with two minors. All three were shot and left for dead in a nearby park, but Santos survived.
Santos will stay in Brazil until Dec. 10 so he can testify at another Candelaria trial.

The National Movement of Streetchildren says four minors are killed every day in Brazil, mostly by police, death squads that often include off-duty police officers or drug gangs. About 90 percent of cases never make it to court.
Emmanuel was sentenced in April to 309 years in prison but had his sentence reduced by 220 years at a retrial. His lawyer hopes a further appeal may bring another reduction.
Under Brazilian law, regardless of sentence, no prisoner may serve more than 30 years.
